title: Giant Configuration Struct (Config coupling)
pattern: A single, massive configuration structure contains every environment variable, credential, and tuning flag for every subsystem in the entire application, and is passed wholesale as a dependency to every class or constructor.
why_bad: It violates interface segregation. A minor configuration change or the addition of a flag for a specific subsystem (e.g., adding an option to the DB configuration) forces re-evaluating and re-compiling all unrelated modules that depend on the giant config, causing unnecessary compilation delay and high change friction.
detection: A struct holding unrelated configuration parameters (e.g., DB URLs alongside email keys) being imported and held by simple, specialized utility classes.
counterexample: A centralized configuration reader that parses the configuration file at the application root and immediately splits and distributes specialized sub-config blocks.
fix: Segregate the configurations. Break down the configuration into small, cohesive structs (`struct SmtpConfig`, `struct DbConfig`) and pass only the relevant, sub-config blocks to the corresponding sub-systems.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 5 ("What should I hide?"); Robert C. Martin, *Clean Architecture* (2017), Chapter 10.
